markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: an attachment that is shown in his artwork.

markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주격 관계대명사 that 뒤에 단수 동사 is가 올바르게 연결되어 선행사인 an attachment를 수식하고 있으므로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 선행사 Santa Fe를 부연 설명하는 관계부사 계속적 용법으로 뒤에 완전한 문장(he worked as a freelance artist)이 이어지므로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): Houser's designs가 주어이며, are modern에 이어서 '뿌리박혀 있다'라는 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사(rooted)가 design을 설명하므로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): '~와 상관없이'라는 의미의 전치사적 어구 regardless of를 구성하는 형용사적 성분으로 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 구조를 분석해 보면 'As a child'는 전치사구이며 이어지는 절에서 'he'가 주어 역할을 하고 있습니다. 한 문장이 성립하기 위해서는 주어에 대응하는 정형동사(Finite Verb)가 반드시 하나 존재해야 하는데, listening을 쓰게 되면 주절의 동사가 없는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 과거 시제의 정형동사인 listened로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다.
keyPoints: (A) 정·준동사 — 주어 뒤에 문장의 중심이 되는 본동사가 필요한 자리인지 판정합니다.
(C) 관계사 — 관계부사 where 뒤에 주어(he)와 동사(worked)를 갖춘 완전한 절이 오는지 판정합니다.
(D) 분사의 능동·수동 — 주어(Houser's designs)와 분사(root)의 관계가 수동이므로 과거분사 형식을 취하는 것이 타당한지 판정합니다.
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he __(A) listening__ to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(C) where__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(D) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, __(E) regardless__ of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 of의 목적어 자리에 동명사 수동태 완료형으로 쓰인 being left는 주어인 '우리(We)'가 홀로 남겨지는 대상이므로 문법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 과거분사 immersed를 뒤에서 수식하는 부사로, '비슷하게 푹 빠진'이라는 의미를 구성하므로 형용사가 아닌 부사 similarly가 오는 것이 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 선행사 a reading group을 수식하며 뒤에 완전한 절(everybody takes turns...)이 이어지므로, 전치사+관계대명사인 in which의 쓰임은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'take turns v-ing'는 '~를 교대로 하다'라는 관용적 표현으로, 준동사 동명사 형태인 reading은 올바른 형태입니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 골격을 살펴보면, other people을 수식하는 관계절이 뒤에 이어지고 있습니다. 밑줄 친 (B)는 선행사인 명사 other people을 수식하면서 동시에 뒤이어 오는 동사구 'are reading'의 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사가 필요한 자리입니다. 따라서 접속사 또는 대명사 지시 관계의 that은 선행사에 수식 관계를 형성할 수 없으며 뒤가 불완전하므로 올 수 없고, 주격 관계대명사인 who나 that(관계사)으로 써야 합니다. 본문에서는 who를 사용하여 선행사 people을 자연스럽게 수식하고 있습니다.
keyPoints: (B) 관계대명사 vs 접속사 — 선행사 유무 및 뒷문장 완전성 판정
(A) 준동사의 태 — 동명사의 수동형(being p.p.) 의미상 주어 판정
(E) 전치사+관계대명사 vs 관계대명사 — 뒤에 이어지는 절의 완전성 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being left__ alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(B) that__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else __(C) similarly__ immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a __(D) reading__ group __(E) in which__ everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (B)

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are something useful produced by a mind.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of their fantastical creatures.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어 technology가 '형체가 없는 무형의 형태로 존재할 수 있다'는 완전한 절을 이끄므로, 장소나 영역의 의미를 가지는 전치사+관계대명사(in which) 또는 관계부사 where의 수식을 받아 완전한 절이 이어지는 구조는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 조건절의 주어는 'a thousand lines'가 아니라 단수 명사구인 'A thousand lines of letters in UNIX' 전체에서 하나의 단위(UNIX로 작성된 1,000행의 문자열)를 나타내므로, 단수 동사인 qualifies가 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): something useful을 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사로, '정신에 의해 만들어진 유용한 것'이라는 수동의 의미적 관계를 형성하므로 produced는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): the multiple overlapping technologies를 수식하는 형용사구 'responsible for ...'의 핵심 형용사로서, 명사 뒤에서 직접 수식하는 구조이므로 형용사 형인 responsible은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 문맥상 '그 소설의 기이한 피조물들(fantastical creatures)'을 의미해야 하므로, 복수 명사인 fantastical creatures를 수식하는 소유격 대명사는 지칭 대상인 'the original novel(원작 소설)'의 수에 일치해야 합니다. 따라서 지칭하는 원작 소설이 단수 명사이므로 복수 소유격 대명사인 their를 단수 소유격 대명사인 its로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 바로 뒤에 복수 명사인 fantastical creatures가 이어져 착각하기 쉽지만, '피조물'들이 갖는 소유 관계의 대상은 소설 한 권이므로 단수형이 올바릅니다.
keyPoints: (E) 대명사의 수일치 — 수식 대상이나 지칭하는 대상의 의미적 단복수를 정확히 구별하여 판정
(B) 주어와 동사의 수일치 — 단위 명사구 전체가 단수 개념을 나타내는지 복수를 나타내는지 구조 분석 필요
(D) 형용사 vs 부사 — 명사 뒤에서 명사를 수식하는 형용사구의 역할을 파악하여 형용사 자리임을 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(B) qualifies__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(C) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(D) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of __(E) their__ fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 선행사 a trait를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that절 내의 동사로, 과거의 역사적 사실이나 지속된 상태를 표현하고 있으므로 과거시제 동사 kept는 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): why가 이끄는 간접의문문 명사절 내에서 동명사 주어 complaining에 호응하는 단수 동사로, 현재의 일반적인 사실을 나타내므로 단수 현재형인 is는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 전치사 by 뒤에 명사적 성격을 가지는 동명사 sharing이 이끄는 동명사구가 위치하여 수단을 올바르게 나타내고 있습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 「the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 ...」 구문으로, 뒤따르는 주절에서 have의 목적어 역할을 하는 reasons가 비교급 형용사 more의 수식을 받아 the more reasons의 형태로 문두로 올바르게 이동하였습니다.

question.explanation: If로 시작하는 조건의 부사절(If you keep a calendar or a journal)이 끝난 뒤에는 주절이 이어져야 하며, 이 주절을 구성할 문장의 정동사(finite verb)가 반드시 필요합니다. 해당 문장에는 주어가 생략된 형태의 명령문이 와야 하므로, 준동사 형태인 making은 주절의 본동사 역할을 할 수 없어 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 making을 명령문을 이끄는 동사원형인 make로 고쳐야 합니다. 많은 학생들이 If절 뒤의 쉼표를 보고 분사구문 등의 준동사 자리가 올 수 있다고 오해하기 쉽지만, 주절 전체의 동사를 확보해야 한다는 문장 구조적 일관성을 기억해야 합니다.
keyPoints: (C) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 부사절 뒤 주절을 이끄는 명령문 동사원형 판단
(A) 동사의 시제와 수일치 — 주격 관계대명사절 내 과거동사의 적절성 판단
(E) 비교구문 — 「the + 비교급, the + 비교급」 구조에서 수식받는 명사의 올바른 위치 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that __(A) kept__ us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining __(B) is__ such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, __(C) making__ a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends __(D) by sharing__ a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the __(E) more reasons__ you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 타동사 'see'의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절을 이끌며, 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 'what'은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 주어 문장의 중심 뼈대는 'The discovery(주어) + [that our memories are reconstructed...](동격절) + completely(부사) + undermining(동사 자리)'의 구조를 가집니다. 주어인 'The discovery'를 수식하는 동격의 'that'절이 'movie'까지 이어지므로, 본문장의 서술어 역할을 할 정동사가 필요합니다. 앞서 제시된 'undermining'은 준동사(현재분사)이므로 주어의 서술어가 될 수 없어 비문입니다. 따라서 과거시제 정동사인 'undermined'로 고쳐야 문장 전체가 완전해집니다.
keyPoints: (E) 정·준동사 — 수식어가 긴 구조에서 문장의 본동사 자리 판정하기
(A) 관계대명사 — 명사절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what의 역할 확인
(C) 분사의 태 — 주어(memories)와의 수동 관계에 따른 과거분사 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode __(A) what__ we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than __(B) storing__ a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are __(C) reconstructed__ through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie __(D) completely__ __(E) undermining__ the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine?

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 빈칭 주어 혹은 형식 주어로 기능하는 비인칭의 'it' 뒤에서 복수 명사구(work commitments and family obligations)에 현혹되지 않고, 문장의 진짜 주어인 단수 'it'에 수일치하여 'feels'를 쓴 것은 동사의 수일치상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 'what if + 주어 + 과거동사' 구문은 현재 사실과 반대되는 가정을 나타내는 부사절 패턴으로, 정동사 자리에 과거형인 'came'을 사용한 것은 자연스럽고 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 'Whether it's'에서 대표/비인칭 단수 주어 'it'에 맞추어 단수 동사 'is'를 선택한 것이며, 뒤에 동명사구 병렬(washing... or taking...)이 이어지더라도 주어인 대명사 'it'과의 일치는 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 병렬이나 비교를 이끄는 'rather than' 뒤에서 명사 상당어구인 동명사구 'viewing chores as...'를 이끄는 'viewing'은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 마지막 문장 'Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores'는 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구입니다. 이 주어부에 이어지는 서술어(본동사)가 필요한 자리에 준동사인 'improving'이 들어가면 문장 전체에 정동사가 존재하지 않는 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 준동사 'improving'을 서술어 역할을 할 수 있는 조동사+동사원형 'can improve'나 정동사 'improves' 등으로 고쳐야 문장 구조가 온전해집니다.
keyPoints: (E) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 문장 전체의 정동사 유무 확인하기
(B) 명사구 삽입과 수일치 — 진짜 주어 'it'과 동사의 단수 수일치
(D) 전치사/접속사 뒤 준동사 — rather than 뒤 동명사 표현의 타당성
question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, making time for exercise __(A) is__ a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often __(B) feels__ like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout __(C) came__ to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than __(D) viewing__ chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores __(E) improving__ your health.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): that절 안의 주어 핵은 단수 명사인 a source이므로, 이에 호응하는 단수 동사has는 수일치상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 주어인 Your auditory areas가 그것의 지속을 '예측하는' 능동의 주체이므로, 과거진행형을 만드는 현재분사 predicting은 어법상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 부사절(as long as ~ didn't change)에 이어지는 주절의 정동사 자리이며, 과거 시점의 사실을 서술하므로 과거동사 paid는 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 동사 stop은 '~하던 것을 멈추다'라는 의미를 나타낼 때 목적어로 동명사를 취하므로 running은 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장의 주절은 people called the police in the middle of the night로 주어(people)와 동사(called)를 갖춘 완전한 절입니다. 접속사 없이 정동사 형태인 claimed를 연결하면 한 문장에 정동사가 두 개 존재하게 되어 문장 구조상 성립하지 않습니다. 해당 자리에는 문장의 주어인 people이 '~라고 주장하면서'라는 능동의 의미를 나타내는 분사구문이 들어가야 하므로, claimed를 능동의 현재분사인 claiming으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.
keyPoints: (E) 정·준동사 — 한 문장 내 정동사 개수 제약과 분사구문의 능동 판단
(A) 수일치 — 수식어가 붙은 주어 명사구의 핵을 찾아 단수/복수 일치 시키기
(D) to-v/v-ing — 동사 stop의 의미 구분에 따른 목적어 형태 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, __(A) has__ just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were __(B) predicting__ its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you __(C) paid__ it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped __(D) running__ elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night __(E) claimed__ that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 사역동사 'has'가 목적어 'us' 뒤에서 목적격 보어로 '목적어가 ~하게 하다'라는 능동적 진행의 의미를 나타낼 때 'piling' 형태로 현재분사를 쓰는 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 문장의 주어 'multitasking'에 수일치하는 3인칭 단수 현재형 정동사이자 타동사 'doesn't save'는 목적어 'any time'을 취하고 있어 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'when done'은 'when it is done'에서 '주어 + be동사'가 생략된 형태로, 세탁기 돌리기(it)는 행해지는 대상이므로 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 'done'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 단수 명사구 'The same'을 주어로 받아 일반 사실을 서술하는 단수 정동사 'applies'는 수일치와 시제가 일치하므로 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 전치사 'to'의 목적어 역할을 하면서 동시에 타동사 'doing'의 목적어 역할을 할 수 있는 명사절 유도 장치가 필요합니다. (C)에 제시된 'that you're doing'에서 'that'이 유도하는 명사절은 뒤에 오는 'doing'의 목적어가 빠져 있어 불완전한 문장 구조를 이룹니다. 접속사 'that'은 뒤에 완전한 절을 이끌어야 하므로 이 자리에는 올 수 없으며, 선행사를 포함하면서 타동사의 목적어 자리를 채울 수 있는 관계대명사 'what'을 사용해 'what you're doing'으로 고쳐야 어법에 맞습니다.
keyPoints: (C) 관계대명사 vs 접속사 — 뒤따르는 절의 문장 성분 완전성 여부로 구성 판정
(A) 목적격보어의 형태 — 사역동사 has가 유발하는 목적어와의 능동·진행 관계 판단
(D) 분사구문의 태 — 생략된 주어와의 능동 및 수동의 동작 관계 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us __(A) piling__ one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking __(B) doesn't save__ any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to __(C) that you're doing__ at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when __(D) done__ with your phone pressed to your ear. The same __(E) applies__ to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수 명사인 a critical factor이므로, 단수 동사 determines를 사용하는 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): the leopard seal을 선행사로 삼고 콤마 뒤에서 이를 계속해서 설명하는 주격 관계대명사의 계속적 용법으로 which를 쓴 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 동사 occurs는 자동사이므로 'The moment (that) occurs'에서 occurs의 주어로 사용된 관계대명사 that은 어법상 적절합니다. (~하는 순간에)
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어 핵인 One penguin's destiny가 3인칭 단수이므로, 단수형 동사 alters는 어법상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: (B) "strolled"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "strolling"로 고쳐야 한다. 문장의 주어인 They는 아델리 펭귄들이며, 펭귄들이 무리 지어 물가로 '거니는 것(stroll)'은 대상이 자발적으로 행하는 능동의 동작입니다. 'find + 목적어 + v-ing(목적어가 ~하는 것을 발견하다)'의 구문이 수동태로 전환된 형태이므로, 목적격 보어 자리에는 능동과 진행을 나타내는 strolling이 그대로 남아야 합니다. 따라서 과거분사인 strolled는 비문이며, strolling으로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 분사 능동 vs 수동 — 의미상 주어(They)와의 능동적 관계 판단
(A) 명사-동사 수일치 — 주격 관계대명사절 내 동사의 수는 선행사의 수에 일치
(C) 관계대명사의 계속적 용법 — 콤마 뒤 선행사 사물/동물을 받는 주격 관계사 which
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor that __(A) determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found __(B) strolled__ in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, __(C) which__ likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment __(D) that__ occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny __(E) alters__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 관계대명사 that의 수식을 받는 선행사인 단수 명사 the distance에 일치하여 단수 형태인 has formed가 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어인 relationships가 유지되는 대상이므로, '수동태(be + 과거분사)' 형태인 aren't kept가 오는 것이 구조상 어법에 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): make sure 뒤에서 명사절을 이끌며 뒤에 완전한 문장 구조(not too much time...)를 동반하는 접속사 that으로 어법상 자연스럽습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 가주어 it에 대응하는 진주어 역할을 하는 명사적 용법의 to부정사 구조로, 부정어 not이 앞에 위치한 not to let 또한 어법상 완전합니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 주절 'We call people...' 뒤에서 주어인 We의 부수적인 상태나 동작을 서술하는 분사구문 자리입니다. We(우리가) 뒤에 나오는 명사절인 목적어(that one small effort...)를 기대하고 바라는 주체이므로 능동의 관계를 나타내야 합니다. 따라서 수동 형태의 과거분사였던 'hoped'를 능동 형태의 현재분사인 'hoping'으로 고쳐야 어법상 올바른 구조가 됩니다.
keyPoints: (B) 분사구문의 능동 vs 수동 — 분사의 의미상 주어가 목적어절을 취하는 능동의 관계이므로 현재분사를 사용
(C) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 주어 주체와 동사 행동 간의 수동적 관계를 파악하여 판단
(E) 가주어-진주어 구문 — 진주어 역할을 수행하는 to부정사의 역할과 부정어의 위치 확인
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
